task.title: Close four vacuity gaps in verify:write-queue block 6 so folder-write serialization is measured directly instead of inferred from lane-map presence
task.objective: scripts/verify-write-queue.mts block 6 asserts that src/storage/folderWriteCoordinator.ts serializes writes per resolved folder, but four of its predicates can pass while the property they name is broken. GAP 1: the same-key continuity check observes the lane map at a single instant, so it cannot distinguish one continuous FIFO generation from a lane that was evicted and recreated between callers; a third same-key caller admitted after the first settles is never exercised. GAP 2: mutual exclusion is inferred from lane-map presence rather than measured, so no assertion would fail if two same-key tasks actually overlapped. GAP 3: nothing catches a coordinator that keeps a lane present but stops advancing its tail, which is the exact shape of a broken chain. GAP 4: block 6g awaits an unbounded Promise.all, so a wedged or rejecting task hangs the verifier or kills the process before the final totals line prints, and the existing bounded settleWithin helper is trapped in 6f-local scope where 6g cannot reach it. This task fixes all four in the verifier only. The production coordinator is believed correct and is touched exclusively as a transient mutation target: every mutant is restored immediately and the file must end this task byte-identical to its recorded original checksum, with the restoration proven by git diff, git status and a re-measured SHA-256. Public coordinator surface (runExclusive, folderCoordinationKey, activeFolderCoordinationKeys) does not grow: no lane-object identity is exposed and no production debug API is added. Existing 6f semantics and the three existing 6g check names are preserved verbatim; assertions are ADDED, never weakened, renamed to a weaker predicate, deleted or made conditional. Every new predicate asserts entry and completion cardinality before any ordering, overlap or FIFO claim, so nothing can pass vacuously over a missing or empty observation set. The task also absorbs the legitimate awkit-wfharden lease-release residue (docs/ai/contracts/active-lease.json, docs/ai/contracts/awkit-wfharden.json, tools/roadmap/assignments.json) through a real closeout rather than a bookkeeping-only task, and reconciles the authoritative project-state sources.

acceptance.description: Block 6g no longer awaits an unbounded Promise.all. The Outcome<T> type and settleWithin helper are hoisted into the smallest scope shared by 6f and 6g, 6f semantics unchanged. A rejecting task becomes a named verifier RED rather than an uncaught top-level rejection, and a wedged task becomes a named timeout RED rather than a hang. In every case the process terminates normally and the final 'Write queue: N/M checks passed' totals line prints. Proven by executing a real rejection/wedge control, not by argument.

A third same-key caller T3, admitted after T1 has settled, is proven to stay on the SAME continuous FIFO serialization chain as T1 and T2: T3 cannot overtake or overlap the already-admitted T2. Entry and completion cardinality for all three callers is asserted before any ordering claim. The Bead's literal wording — an external caller executing strictly between T1 settling and T2 starting — is adjudicated against live Promise reaction ordering and the source-backed correction is recorded rather than a fabricated timing-window test being written. Proven RED by a real premature lane eviction/recreation mutation in the coordinator, chosen so the old one-instant lane-presence assertion can remain superficially plausible while the new three-caller invariant catches the defect.

Same-key mutual exclusion is MEASURED, not inferred from lane-map presence. The verifier records per-caller enter/exit events (or equivalent intervals) and asserts separately: every expected caller entered; every expected caller exited; event cardinality is exactly correct; the maximum same-key active count is exactly 1; no two same-key execution intervals intersect; ordering is FIFO where required. Proven RED by a real coordinator mutation that permits overlap, with the exact final verifier count and the exact failing assertion names recorded.

A coordinator that keeps the lane present but stops advancing the lane tail is caught. The mutation removes or bypasses the live equivalent of owned.tail = settled, leaving lane-map presence superficially plausible while new callers no longer chain to the prior task. The record states which old lane-presence assertions stayed GREEN, which new direct serialization assertion went RED, the exact totals, and that the run terminated normally. This is the required proof that map presence is not being used as a proxy for serialization.

SOURCE-BACKED CORRECTION TO THE BEAD'S LITERAL WORDING, recorded in scripts/verify-write-queue.mts rather than fabricated as a test. The Bead asks for an external caller executing strictly between T1 settling and T2 starting. That window is not reachable. In runExclusive, an arriving caller captures `const owned = lane;` (line 132) and installs `owned.tail.then(runTask, runTask)` (line 143) SYNCHRONOUSLY at admission, so T2's reaction is already registered on T1's settled promise before T1 finishes. Promise reactions registered earlier drain as microtasks before any later macrotask can run, so no externally scheduled caller can interleave into that gap; and an already-admitted T2 stays chained regardless of any later map mutation, because it holds a direct reference to the lane object rather than re-reading the map. A test claiming to occupy that window would be timing fiction. The invariant that IS decidable, and is what the new block 6h asserts, is that T1, T2 and a later-arriving T3 on the same key remain on one continuous FIFO serialization chain and that T3 can neither overtake nor overlap the already-admitted T2. Mutant M1 confirms the adjudication empirically: with eviction moved to the first settle, the fresh-generation defect appears exactly where the analysis predicts — at the LATER arrival T3, never at the already-admitted T2.

completion.notes: REVIEWER INDEPENDENCE DISCLOSURE. This repository runs in single-agent mode (CONCURRENCY_POLICY.defaultMode = single-agent, routineSubagents = 0, tools/agents/context-policy.mjs), so the same primary agent implemented the verifier change, ran QA and performed the QC review. That is not organizational independence and is not claimed to be. What is claimed is method independence: the QC pass started from the diff (git diff -- scripts/verify-write-queue.mts, 458 insertions / 33 deletions) and from the contract's acceptance criteria, not from the implementation narrative, and every QC conclusion below is checked against the diff text or against a measured run rather than against recollection. Same disclosure pattern as docs/ai/contracts/awkit-glm-delegation-tooling.json. QC CHRONOLOGY, disclosed because it is unusual. qc_status had to be recorded APPROVED before the FIRST lease release of this task, not after the last one. finalizeLease in tools/agents/lease.mjs refuses to release a lease carrying an unresolved violation unless the path appears in approvedOverridePaths, and approvedOverridePaths returns an empty set unless contract.completion.qc_status === 'APPROVED'. Every lease transition funnels through finalizeLease - a plain release, and also an amendment that reroutes to another holder - so with the .beads/interactions.jsonl violation recorded, no further lease rotation of any kind was reachable until this field was set. QC pass 1 was therefore performed at that point, on the COMPLETE and frozen verifier work: all four gaps implemented, all five mutants applied and restored, verify:write-queue measured green at 78/78, and the coordinator digest re-measured identical to baseline. Nothing about scripts/verify-write-queue.mts changed after QC pass 1. QC pass 2 covers the work that came after the release - the tracker pin move in scripts/verify-roadmap-dashboard.mjs and the four project-state narratives - and is recorded in the qc-final evidence item. QC PASS 1 FINDINGS. Confirmed by reading the diff: the totals line exists at exactly one call site (finish()), and the three ways the file can end - normal completion, the RUN_DEADLINE_MS backstop, an escaped rejection or exception - all route through it, so no termination path can drop the Write queue N/M line; the backstop timer is deliberately not unref'd and is cleared by finish(), so it neither costs a green run time nor lets a wedge vanish; settleWithin attaches a no-op catch to the raced promise before racing it, so the abandoned branch of a timeout cannot surface as an unhandled rejection, and its timer is cleared on both outcomes; settleAllWithin is Promise.all over settleWithin, which never rejects, so one wedged or rejecting member cannot strand the others; spansOf returns null rather than a shorter array on any missing, duplicated or malformed observation, and every predicate that quantifies over spans is guarded by an explicit cardinality check first, which is the specific defect shape recorded in KNOWN_ISSUES for .every() over a dropped observation; the 6i control runs the same recorder, the same pairing and the same overlap predicate over four deliberately un-serialized folders and requires strictly positive overlap and peak occupancy equal to the caller count, so a blind instrument fails the control instead of silently passing the six assertions above it; and the control's own body races allArrived against a bounded drain, so a coordinator that wrongly serialized the control would red it rather than wedge the run. NON-BLOCKING QC OBSERVATION, recorded rather than silently fixed: the GAP 4 rationale comment reads 'Without a deadline that ends one of two ways' where a comma after 'deadline' is intended. It is a punctuation slip in a comment, it changes no predicate and no behaviour, and correcting it would require rotating a QA lease back onto a file whose mutation evidence is already frozen and whose digest is already recorded. Disposition: accepted as-is, disclosed here, not counted as a defect against any acceptance criterion. QC PASS 1 VERDICT: APPROVED for scripts/verify-write-queue.mts and for the emergency override recorded in write_lease.overrides[0].
